name: @browzer/skills
description: AI agent skills for Browzer — hybrid vector + Graph RAG for codebases and document workspaces. Skills around the `browzer` CLI: RAG search, dependency graph, doc ingestion, workspace management, and a tier-aware end-to-end dev pipeline (brainstorming → probe-tier → generate-prd → scope-feature → generate-task → execute-task → code-review → receiving-code-review → regression-guard → feature-acceptance → finalize-feature → commit). A haiku probe at orchestrator Step 0.5 picks `tier ∈ {express, standard, full}` per feat; express skips PRD/scope/task-plan entirely. State lives as plain markdown under `docs/browzer/<feat>/staging/` (six per-phase subfolders: planning/, tasks/, review/, review-lanes/, fixes/, acceptance/), gitignored; only `README.md` at the feat root is committed. Code-review spawns 4 mandatory Opus lanes (senior-engineer, software-architect, qa, regression-tester) + a cheap haiku pr-coherence lane + N dynamic specialists; the regression-tester scopes to baseline-failure detection against `main` via git-stash. Mutation testing is removed entirely (operational reliability was below the bar). Tests are authored inline by `execute-task`'s coder alongside the implementation; a hard-fail host quality gate (lint + typecheck + test; + build at tier=full when public API drifted) runs BEFORE the TASK atomic-renames to .completed.md. Receiving-code-review closes EVERY finding with a 7-step ladder for zero-tech-debt by default. A new `regression-guard` skill re-runs the host quality gate over the aggregate post-fix diff, routing failures back through the fix ladder for up to 3 rounds. Feature-acceptance mode is tier-aware (smoke / hybrid / autonomous-with-stack-boot). Finalize-feature absorbs both host-doc patching (Phase A) and the committed README render (Phase B). Universal subagent preamble requires `browzer deps --reverse` blast-radius probing before edits.
